scenes.spoken: Every day, regulated organisations decide who may see what. Qadamar makes each of those decisions, explains it, and records it.
Each request passes nine checks, always in the same order: from role, through classification and need-to-know, to context and separation of duty. A single deny stops it.

Government. Case files carry a classification and compartments. An analyst cleared to L two searches the archive: L three files never appear, not even their titles. And off the trusted network, the reachable level drops.

Banking. The officer who creates a payment cannot approve it, or release it. Release runs as a certified command, with a single-use, signed token. And a document carrying account numbers is never exported.

Healthcare. A clinician sees the records of the patients they treat, and nothing else. In an emergency, the glass can be broken, with a reason, for four hours at most. An alert goes out, and someone else reviews it.

Enterprise CRM. A project manager opens a contract: the client, the scope, the milestones. The amounts come back masked, because they carry the finance class. A finance approver opens the same contract and sees them. And if the mask cannot be applied, nothing is released.
Every rule change shows its impact first, and needs a second approver. And every decision lands in a hash-chained log that an auditor can verify.
Qadamar. Self-hosted access control for regulated organisations.
